translations.answer: Kajita 2003 formulates walking-pattern generation as ZMP tracking. Under the paper's parameters, a 1.6-second preview lets the center of mass respond before support exchange, while a 0.8-second preview is insufficient. The reusable result is the structure of future-reference feedforward, current-state feedback, and model-error correction—not a robot-independent 1.6-second constant or a complete hardware-stability guarantee.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Future foothold timing and ZMP reference are known over a finite horizon.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: The 3D-LIPM/cart-table approximation and fixed-height assumptions are acceptable as a nominal planner.
translations.applicability.controllers.1: Downstream whole-body inverse kinematics and control
translations.applicability.environments.0: Planned biped walking with prescribed footholds
translations.applicability.robots.0: HRP-2P model in the paper; other robots require new gains and validation
translations.confidence_rationale: The derivation and 1.6 s versus 0.8 s preview comparison directly isolate the future-reference mechanism, and the multibody correction experiment quantifies nominal-model error reduction. Confidence is capped because the spiral-stair result is simulation-only, official code is unavailable, and the model omits several hardware constraints.
translations.evidence.0.note: Derives integral, state, and preview feedback; compares preview horizons; quantifies multibody ZMP correction; and reports only simulated spiral-stair walking.
translations.evidence.0.title: Biped Walking Pattern Generation by Using Preview Control of Zero-Moment Point
translations.evidence.1.note: Records that no version-pinned author implementation was found, limiting claims about code-level reproducibility.
translations.evidence.1.title: Kajita 2003 ZMP preview-control official-code status
translations.terms.1: Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU, 惯性测量单元)
